basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/Intel471/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The Intel 471 solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests malware indicators from Intel 471's Verity 471 or Titan API into the Log Analytics workspace, and provides a curated set of community hunting queries to proactively hunt for threats in Microsoft Sentinel. **Hunting Queries:** 25, **Playbooks:** 1 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: AnyDesk Execution from Abnormal Folder - Potential Malicious Use of RMM Tool

options.text: AnyDesk is a legitimate remote control tool widely abused by actors to access victim machines and deploy malware or ransomware. This hunt excludes common AnyDesk install paths, surfacing execution from directories such as Temp, ProgramData or System32. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery2
elements.label: AnyDesk Service Installation - Potentially Malicious RMM Tool Installation

options.text: Identifies when the AnyDesk service is installed onto a system. This can be legitimate if the organization allows AnyDesk, however if it is not a commonly utilized application, any service installations should be considered suspect. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvents Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery3
elements.label: Autorun or ASEP Registry Key Modification

options.text: Adversaries and malware persist by adding a program to the startup folder or a Registry run key, so it runs at user logon. Run keys have legitimate uses, but malicious entries often have random names or load objects from temp or public folders. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery4
elements.label: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Discovery

options.text: This Hunt Package identifies activity that could be associated with discovery behaviors targeting AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). This hunting query depends on AWS data connector (AWSCloudTrail Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery5
elements.label: Browser Spawning Suspicious Applications - Potential Exploit or Social Engineering

options.text: Browser exploitation often ends in a command being run. This hunt covers scripting engines and other applications a browser can be abused to launch, including the FileFix technique that tricks a user into pasting an attacker command into File Explorer. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery6
elements.label: Creating a Shadow Copy

options.text: This Threat Hunt package identifies suspicious activities related shadow copies being created from a variety of techniques. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery7
elements.label: Dump LSASS via Renamed procdump

options.text: Identify ProcDump usage as a means to dump LSASS data. ProcDump is a SysInternals tool that can be used to dump process memory, dumping the process memory of lsass.exe which can be used to obtain credentials. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery8
elements.label: Execution BAT Script to Unpack Payload

options.text: This Hunt Package is meant to identify a nuanced method of execution of a .bat file that can be indicative of an unpacking sequence that leads to the deployment of an additional executable. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery9
elements.label: File Created In Startup Folder

options.text: This package is designed to detect the activity around a file being created and put in the Windows Startup Folder. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery10
elements.label: Java Spawning Child Process by Unique Child Process Name - Potential Exploitation Activity

options.text: Identifies child processes spawned by Java, ordered by the most unique parent/child pair first, to surface outliers that may indicate exploitation. Legitimate results are expected. Inspired by the Log4Shell, Spring4Shell and Text4Shell vulnerabilities. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery11
elements.label: MeshAgent Suspicious Child Process - Potential Malicious RMM Tool Usage

options.text: Identifies the default installation process executing suspect applications, such as powershell, schtasks, cmd and other applications that can by abused by built in modules. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery12
elements.label: Methods for Downloading Files with PowerShell

options.text: Identifies PowerShell downloading files from external sources, a common malware delivery technique. Covers Invoke-WebRequest, Invoke-RestMethod and Start-BitsTransfer, the curl and wget aliases, and .NET classes System.Net.WebClient and HttpClient. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery13
elements.label: NetSupport Manager Execution from Abnormal Folder - Potential Malicious Use of RMM Tool

options.text: NetSupport is a legitimate remote control tool, and the base of the NetSupport RAT, abused to access victim machines and deploy malware. This hunt excludes common install paths, surfacing execution from directories such as Temp or System32. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery14
elements.label: Potential Maldoc Execution Chain Observed

options.text: Detects the aftermath of a successfully executed Microsoft Office maldoc: a document opened from an email or download spawns a suspicious execution and attempts to run code via common Windows binaries such as powershell, cmd or rundll32. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery15
elements.label: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution

options.text: Looks for variations of the PowerShell -EncodedCommand parameter, commonly used to obfuscate commands. Not all occurrences are malicious, so base64 decode the command for analysis. Tune noisy results by grouping on parent process or rare commands. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents MicrosoftThreatProtection data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent DeviceEvents Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery16
elements.label: Powershell History Modification or Deletion

options.text: Adversaries may attempt to clear the command history of compromised hosts to conceal the actions that they have performed during an attack. This content will detect if PowerShell's history was cleared, disabled, or modified. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery17
elements.label: Python Executing from Non-Standard Directory

options.text: This Threat Hunt package identifies suspicious Python executions originating from non-standard directories, such as hidden or unconventional locations signaling potential malware infection. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery18
elements.label: Remote Atera Agent Download - Command Line

options.text: This Threat Hunt package identifies when a tool like a lolbin is used to fetch the Atera's Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) agent directly from Atera's distribution domain. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery19
elements.label: Scheduled Task Executing from Abnormal Location

options.text: This hunt package is designed to capture activity associated with a scheduled task which includes abnormal locations in its details for execution. This is often a mark of persistence or malicious tasks created by malware or attackers. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery20
elements.label: Shadow Copies Deletion Using Operating Systems Utilities

options.text: Ransomware commonly deletes Windows shadow copies before encrypting data on the victim host. This hunt identifies powershell, wmic, vssadmin or vssvc executing with command line arguments containing delete and variations of shadow. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery21
elements.label: Suspect Child Process to IIS Worker Process (w3wp.exe) - Potential Exploitation

options.text: Identifies abnormal child processes of the Microsoft IIS Worker Process (w3wp.exe), which runs Web applications and handles requests for an application pool. Children such as cmd.exe or powershell.exe can indicate an exploit attempt. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery22
elements.label: Suspicious Child Process for Java - Potential Exploitation Activity

options.text: Identifies Java spawning unusual child processes, which can indicate exploitation of the Java process. Java may not be the exploit target itself, but can be coaxed into executing malicious code via another service, such as Log4j or Spring-Core. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery23
elements.label: User Added to Default Privileged Windows Security Groups

options.text: This package is designed to capture the activity surrounding the execution of command line arguments that add a user to default privileged Windows Security Groups (local and domain). This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery24
elements.label: Wevtutil Cleared Log

options.text: This use case is designed to detect when "wevtutil" is used to clear logs to potentially obfuscate malicious events occurring prior to the clean up. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery25
elements.label: WMIC Windows Internal Discovery and Enumeration

options.text: This will identify the potentially malicious use of WMI (Windows Management Interface) utilized for local enumeration and discovery of a host. This hunting query depends on SecurityEvents WindowsSecurityEvents data connector (SecurityEvent SecurityEvent Parser or Table)
